must_fix.issue: Advisor slogan reads as generic marketing on an otherwise careful page. r2 line 165: "If you would rather have one person plan the venue, travel and vendors around your marriage office dates, [speak with a Wedded Advisor](/wonderland-concierge), who stays with you from the first idea to the last dance."
must_fix.fix: Cut "who stays with you from the first idea to the last dance". Use only brand-facts.md "Claims we can make", e.g. "...[speak with a Wedded Advisor](/wonderland-concierge), your single point of contact from start to finish, who confirms inclusions and the fee in writing before you commit." No phone line, senior planner, scale or marriage-office booking claims.

must_fix.issue: Unfinished-sounding phrasing on a custom guests ask about. r2 line 117: "We did not find a cultural or academic source for its details in time for this guide, so we leave the specifics to your families, who will know how they do it."
must_fix.fix: Plain statement, no new facts: "We found no cultural or academic source for its details, so we leave the specifics to your families, who will know how they do it."

should_fix.issue: No word for older or less mobile guests when peak months are named. r2 line 33: "GoTürkiye names May, August and September as the most popular months for weddings. <!-- fact_04 --> If you are flying guests in from Australia, factor those months into your dates early."
should_fix.fix: Add one line framed as venue questions, no climate figures: "If older or less mobile guests are coming, ask each venue about shade, step-free access and transfers from the hotel before you choose a date."

should_fix.issue: Music-rules line stops short for large or multi-day celebrations. r2 line 105: "That carrying sound is the point. For a hotel or villa arrival, check the venue's music rules first."
should_fix.fix: Turn into venue questions with no scale claim: "...check the venue's music rules first, and ask whether exclusive use is available if you want the henna night and the wedding under one roof."

consider.issue: 'Well before you fly' gives no plannable lead time. r2 line 19: "For Australians, the legal marriage goes through a municipal marriage office in Türkiye, and the paperwork, including a certified certificate of eligibility to marry, should start well before you fly."
consider.fix: Do not invent a timeframe. Leave wording as is, or add "[[VERIFY: typical lead time for CNI and apostille for Türkiye, per DFAT or the Turkish embassy]]" and carry it to verify_items. Deferred, not a blocker.
